tutorial.title: Python Modules
tutorial.descriptionContent: Recall and apply module, multi-file program, and package skills through interleaved practice.

lessons.title: Choose a Focused Module
lessons.interactiveContent:
Which module keeps one clear responsibility for a transit app?

route_guides.py stores route lookup functions and route constantstools.py stores routes, account settings, and ticket messagesscript.py copies every route function used by the app

route_guides.py stores route lookup functions and route constants.
lessons.hardModeContent:
route_guides.py handles route lookup. You add account preferences. Which plan keeps one clear job per module?

Keep route lookup in route_guides.py and put account preferences in accounts.py.Add preferences to route_guides.py because both features belong to the transit app.Move both features to helpers.py because both contain reusable functions.

Keep route lookup in route_guides.py and put account preferences in accounts.py.

lessons.title: Assign Each File a Job
lessons.interactiveContent:
Which file plan gives each part of a meal app one clear job?

script.py coordinates, portions.py calculates servings, and labels.py formats textscript.py contains every functionEvery file keeps a copy of the serving calculation

script.py coordinates, portions.py calculates servings, and labels.py formats text.
lessons.hardModeContent:
script.py coordinates, portions.py calculates servings, and labels.py formats text. You change only meal wording. Where?

Change labels.py while keeping the serving calculation in portions.py.Move serving calculations into labels.py and change both there.Copy the label formatting into script.py and update that copy.

Change labels.py while keeping the serving calculation in portions.py.

lessons.title: Import the Route Module
lessons.interactiveContent:
Complete the import for the sibling module route_guides.py.

Make sure to pick route_guides.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Complete the import for the sibling module route_guides.py.

Make sure to pick import, followed by route_guides, and finally DEFAULT_ROUTE.

lessons.title: Keep script.py Coordinating
lessons.interactiveContent:
Which work belongs in the entry file script.py?

Import the reusable modules, call a provided function, and display the resultDefine every function that the program needsDefine every constant that the program needs

Import the reusable modules, call a provided function, and display the result.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Two entry files need the same route calculation. How should script.py keep its coordinating job?

Keep the calculation in a reusable module; import it, call it and display its result.Define the calculation in script.py and make the second entry file import script.py.Copy the calculation into both entry files so each can run alone.

Keep the calculation in a reusable module; import it, call it and display its result.

lessons.title: Find the __init__.py Role
lessons.interactiveContent:
What does package/__init__.py do in a given package?

It marks the package surface and can expose selected modulesIt replaces every module in the packageIt tells Python who authored the package

It marks the package surface and can expose selected modules.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Your package contains totals.py and labels.py. You want its package import to expose only totals. What should you do?

Use from . import totals in the package __init__.py.Move all of totals.py into __init__.py and delete the module.Make __init__.py run both modules as entry files.

Use from . import totals in the package __init__.py.

lessons.title: Call Through the Namespace
lessons.interactiveContent:
Use the imported namespace to call next_stop().

Make sure to pick route_guides.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Use the imported namespace to call next_stop().

Make sure to pick import, followed by route_guides, and finally next_stop.

lessons.title: Pass the Meal Inputs
lessons.interactiveContent:
Add the second parameter so the function receives all data explicitly.

Make sure to pick attendees.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Pass attendees per group as the second parameter. Return the total servings for all groups using the two inputs.

Make sure to pick attendees, followed by groups, and finally *.

lessons.title: Expose a Report Module
lessons.interactiveContent:
Given a package for reporting, which line belongs in report_tools/__init__.py to expose summaries?

from . import summariesimport . summariesfrom summaries import package

from . import summaries.
lessons.hardModeContent:
report_tools/__init__.py exposes summaries. You add charts.py beside it. Which replacement exposes both modules?

from . import summaries, chartsfrom .summaries import chartsfrom charts import summaries

from . import summaries, charts.

lessons.title: Import One Fare Function
lessons.interactiveContent:
Import only zone_fare() from fares.py.

Make sure to pick from followed by fares and then import, zone_fare.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Import only zone_fare() from fares.py and choose the number of zones that makes the result 6.

Make sure to pick from, followed by fares, import, zone_fare, and finally 3.

lessons.title: Find the Hidden Global
lessons.interactiveContent:
Why is this module harder to reuse by itself?

It depends on meal_data.guest_count instead of receiving the countIt returns a calculated valueIts function has a descriptive name

It depends on meal_data.guest_count instead of receiving the count.
lessons.hardModeContent:
You need two groups with five guests each, without changing meal_data. Which change makes the function reusable?

Add a guest_count parameter, multiply by it, and call total_servings(2, 5).Call total_servings(5) and leave the function unchanged.Set guest_count to 5 in script.py and leave portions.py unchanged.

Add a guest_count parameter, multiply by it, and call total_servings(2, 5).

lessons.title: Read the Public Surface
lessons.interactiveContent:
The file report_tools/__init__.py contains from . import summaries. Which module is exposed to the public?

summaries.pyscript.pyexports.py

Make sure to pick summaries.py.
lessons.hardModeContent:
report_tools/__init__.py uses from . import summaries. You change it to from . import summaries, charts. What is exposed?

Both summaries and charts.Only charts, because it replaces the earlier name.Only summaries, because the second name is ignored.

Both summaries and charts.

lessons.title: Select Two Module Names
lessons.interactiveContent:
Add the constant to this selective import, then read both imported names in use.

Make sure to type DAY_PASS.

lessons.title: Import the Whole Package
lessons.interactiveContent:
Which import keeps report_tools in the caller's namespace, so you can call something like report_tools.generate_report() afterward?

import report_toolsfrom report_tools import summariesimport report_tools.summaries

import report_tools.
lessons.hardModeContent:
report_tools exposes summaries. You replace from report_tools import summaries with import report_tools. Which name reaches that module?

report_tools.summariessummariesreport_tools.generate_report

Make sure to pick report_tools.summaries.

lessons.title: Compare Import Styles
lessons.interactiveContent:
Which import makes next_stop() available as a direct name, so you can call it simply as next_stop() afterward?

from route_guides import next_stopimport route_guidesimport route_guides.next_stop

from route_guides import next_stop.
lessons.hardModeContent:
You replace import route_guides with from route_guides import next_stop. Which call uses the new direct name for "Museum"?

next_stop("Museum")route_guides.next_stop("Museum")next_stop.route_guides("Museum")

Make sure to pick next_stop("Museum").

lessons.title: Point Imports One Way
lessons.interactiveContent:
Which import direction keeps the entry file in charge?

script.py imports portions.py, and portions.py receives parametersscript.py imports portions.py, and portions.py imports script.pyBoth files import each other and share globals

script.py imports portions.py, and portions.py receives parameters.
lessons.hardModeContent:
script.py imports portions.py. You pass the guest count as a parameter and remove its need to read the entry file. Which plan fits?

Keep script importing portions; portions does not import script.Make portions import script instead, so portions starts the calculation.Keep imports in both directions, but delay one until the function runs.

Keep script importing portions; portions does not import script.

lessons.title: Choose the Package Import
lessons.interactiveContent:
Which import lets the code call summary(12) directly?

from report_tools.summaries import summaryimport report_toolsimport report_tools.summaries

from report_tools.summaries import summary.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Which import lets the code call summary(12) directly?

from report_tools.summaries import summaryimport report_toolsfrom report_tools import summaries

from report_tools.summaries import summary.

lessons.title: Break the Import Circle
lessons.interactiveContent:
The output confirms that portions.py imports script.py while script.py imports portions.py. How can the app remove this circular dependency?

Remove the script import from portions.py and pass guest_count as a parameterImport script.py again inside portions.pyCopy the entry-file code into portions.py

Remove the script import from portions.py and pass guest_count as a parameter.
lessons.hardModeContent:
The shown imports form a circle. You remove import script from portions.py. What else must change to keep its calculation working?

Add a guest_count parameter and use it in place of script.guest_count.Keep script.guest_count because script.py already defines it.Move import script inside servings() and keep script.guest_count.

Add a guest_count parameter and use it in place of script.guest_count.

lessons.title: Spot the Import Side Effect
lessons.interactiveContent:
What happens when script.py imports this module?

The module displays Demo while Python imports itOnly the function definition loadsThe demo waits for a call from script.py

The module displays Demo while Python imports it.
lessons.hardModeContent:
You remove the bottom show_demo() call, leaving the function definition unchanged. What happens when script.py imports it?

Nothing prints, and route_guides.show_demo remains available to call.Demo still prints because importing runs the function body.The import fails because the module no longer calls its function.

Nothing prints, and route_guides.show_demo remains available to call.

lessons.title: Name the Module Safely
lessons.interactiveContent:
Which filename clearly describes menu selection helpers without potentially overriding a Python standard-library module?

menu_tools.pyrandom.pymath.py

Make sure to pick menu_tools.py.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Your menu helpers are in a local random.py, hiding the standard module. You rename it to menu_tools.py. How should the app reach them?

Import menu_tools and use menu_tools for the helper calls.Keep import random and random helper calls because renaming the file changes no imports.Rename the helper to math.py and import math to avoid the random name.

Import menu_tools and use menu_tools for the helper calls.

lessons.title: Classify Module Sources
lessons.interactiveContent:
Which list correctly classifies the three modules?

company_reports is project code, math is Python standard-library code, and tabulate is an installed external dependencyAll three modules must be in the current projectThe import keyword changes with each module's author

company_reports is project code, math is Python standard-library code, and tabulate is an installed external dependency.
lessons.hardModeContent:
company_reports is in your project, math comes with Python, and tabulate is installed in your active environment.

Python can find all three. What follows when you import them?

The same import keyword works for all three sources.Only company_reports can be imported because only it is a project file.tabulate needs the module author in its import because it is external.

The same import keyword works for all three sources.

lessons.title: Match the __name__ Value
lessons.interactiveContent:
What is __name__ inside route_guides.py when script.py imports it?

route_guides__main__script

Make sure to pick route_guides.
lessons.hardModeContent:
You first run route_guides.py directly, then import it from script.py in a new run. What is its __name__ in each case?

Direct run: __main__; import: route_guides.Direct run: route_guides; import: __main__.Direct run: __main__; import: script.

Direct run: __main__; import: route_guides.

lessons.title: Check What Imports Need
lessons.interactiveContent:
What must be true before Python can import a project, standard-library, or installed module?

Python can find the module in the project, standard library, or active environmentThe import names the module's authorEvery module uses a different import keyword

Python can find the module in the project, standard library, or active environment.
lessons.hardModeContent:
A teammate can import an external module, but Python cannot find it in your active environment. What must change before your import works?

Make the module available where your Python environment can find it.Add your teammate as the author in the import statement.Replace import with from while leaving the module unavailable.

Make the module available where your Python environment can find it.

lessons.title: Complete the Main Guard
lessons.interactiveContent:
Complete the value that makes the demo run only when this module runs directly.

Make sure to pick __main__.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Complete the guard so the demo runs only when this module runs directly.

Make sure to pick if, followed by __name__, ==, and finally __main__.

lessons.title: Trace the Meal Data
lessons.interactiveContent:
Which sequence matches this program's data flow?

script.py sends values to portions.py, passes its result to labels.py, then displays the labellabels.py starts script.py and changes a shared totalportions.py imports script.py before returning a global

script.py sends values to portions.py, passes its result to labels.py, then displays the label.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Which sequence matches this program's data flow?

script.py sends values to portions.py, passes its result to labels.py, then displays the labellabels.py starts script.py and changes a shared totalportions.py reads its inputs from script.py while labels.py edits a shared total

script.py sends values to portions.py, passes its result to labels.py, then displays the label.

lessons.title: Choose the Clean Module
lessons.interactiveContent:
Which design keeps route helpers reusable without unwanted import output?

route_guides.py contains route helpers and guards its demo call with a main guardroute_guides.py prints a demo at the top level whenever it is importedroute_guides.py also stores account settings and payment messages

route_guides.py contains route helpers and guards its demo call with a main guard.
lessons.hardModeContent:
You want imports to stay quiet but still provide show_demo(). Direct runs should display the demo. Where should the main guard go?

Keep the definition outside the guard and put only the demo call inside it.Put both the function definition and call inside the guard.Guard the function definition but leave the demo call outside it.

Keep the definition outside the guard and put only the demo call inside it.
